features.name: Soudan Mine shaft house (surface)

provenance.note: OpenStreetMap alone yields at most 'approximate' confidence (contract §1.2). Surface shaft house; not a claim about the Level 27 cavern's own footprint (see geometry:soudan-minos-far-detector-point).

features.method: Derived: a rectangle in plan, 8 m wide (the 'edge to edge dimension of 8 m' of the octagonal steel planes) and 30.31 m long, centred on the surveyed midpoint of the two supermodules (47.820267 N, 92.241412 W) and aligned with the published detector and cavern axis, azimuth 333.4452° (26.5548° west of true north). Along the axis it runs from 15.631 m upstream of the midpoint ('The origin of the detector coordinate system is the upstream edge of the far detector. This lies 15.631 m upstream from the midpoint') to 14.675 m downstream (half of the 1.15 m gap plus the 14.10 m second supermodule); the first supermodule is 14.78 m long. Computed on a local equirectangular plane. Inputs are all from arXiv:0805.3170 Secs. 1, 6.5 (survey precision 0.7 m per coordinate, axis 15 microradians); accuracy_m 3 m also covers the steel-envelope definition. The coil ends, cosmic-ray veto shield and walkways are not included; this is the steel-and-scintillator stack, not the cavern.
features.name: MINOS far detector steel-plane envelope (plan view, derived from the published survey)

provenance.locator: arXiv:0805.3170 Sec. 1 (planes 8 m edge to edge; supermodules 14.78 m and 14.10 m; 1.15 m gap) and Sec. 6.5 (midpoint coordinate, 15.631 m, azimuth 333.4452°)
provenance.note: Derived from a surveyed point, a surveyed azimuth and published dimensions; every input is quoted in method. No independent figure measures the footprint itself, so there is no checks[] row.
provenance.quote: The far detector and cavern axes are level and at an azimuth of 333.4452° (26.5548° west of true north).

features.method: Point coordinate taken directly from the MINOS detector paper (arXiv:0805.3170 Sec. 6.5): the midpoint between the two far-detector supermodules, surveyed at latitude 47.820267 N, longitude 92.241412 W (NAD 83), 705 m below the surface. Inertial survey precision 0.7 m per coordinate; accuracy_m 3 m rounds that up. The five-decimal value in PRD 76, 052003 agrees to 0.3 m.
features.name: Soudan Underground Laboratory, Level 27 (MINOS far detector, CDMS II, SuperCDMS Soudan)

provenance.note: 'verified' because representation is 'surveyed' from a rank <=10 source (A15/A25). The six-decimal survey of the MINOS detector paper replaces the five-decimal value of the PRD 76, 052003 paper (47.82027 N, 92.24141 W, 0.3 m apart). It is the midpoint between the two supermodules, referenced to the surface by an inertial survey (University of Calgary, April 1999) with a precision of 0.7 m per coordinate; the paper also gives the Fermilab-to-Soudan vector to better than 1 cm horizontally.
provenance.quote: That midpoint was surveyed and determined to be located at latitude 47.820267 degrees north, longitude 92.241412 degrees west, and ellipsoid height -248.4 m in North American Datum 1983 (NAD 83).

features.method: OpenStreetMap way 1293533760 (man_made=mineshaft, name 'Shaft #8', area=yes, 44 m2) kept verbatim. Which mine shaft carries the laboratory's cages is not stated in the fetched sources; arXiv:0805.3170 Sec. 6.4.1 says only that equipment goes down 'a relatively small shaft dating to the days of iron mining' that 'is inclined by 12° with respect to the vertical'.
features.name: Soudan Mine 'Shaft #8' (OpenStreetMap)

provenance.note: OpenStreetMap alone yields at most 'approximate'; the link to the laboratory is not established, so the feature is context only.

summary.plain: The Soudan iron mine in northern Minnesota, with the historic shaft house at the surface and, 705 m down on the 27th level, the MINOS far detector drawn at its surveyed position and orientation. The cavern and the neighbouring dark-matter laboratory are not located.

unlocated.backlog: The MINOS TDR (NuMI-L-337) or a Soudan lab level-27 plan giving the cavern dimensions and the offset between the MINOS and Soudan 2 / CDMS caverns; with the published axis azimuth the MINOS hall can be drawn as a rectangle about the surveyed midpoint, and the neighbouring cavern placed from the stated offset.
unlocated.reason: The cavern that houses MINOS and the neighbouring Soudan laboratory (the former Soudan 2 cavern, CDMS II, SuperCDMS Soudan) are named in the MINOS paper ('the MINOS detector hall and the neighboring Soudan laboratory') but their sizes and positions relative to the surveyed detector midpoint are not given in any fetched source: the paper states only the detector/cavern axis azimuth. The MINOS Technical Design Report (OSTI 1861363; Fermilab archive) and the University of Minnesota laboratory site, which may carry cavern dimensions and a level plan, were unreachable (HTTP 403 and connection refused).
